The earliest known computational device
is the abacus, which emerged around 2400
BCE in Mesopotamia. The abacus functioned
as a counting frame and was used primarily
for arithmetic operations. Its design varied
across different cultures, such as the Chinese
suanpan and the Roman hand abacus. Despite
its simplicity, the abacus set the foundation for
systematic numerical computation, enabling
societies to handle commerce, taxation, and
engineering more effectively.
